changes.current_line: Online and in-store on one platform; the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
changes.change: For retail buyers with stores (especially COO and store-operations audiences): "One system for the tills and the website: one customer, one basket. An order bought online can be returned at any store till, and the loyalty record follows the customer." Say "the tills," not "point of sale" or "in-person payments," with this audience. Back the claim with a live till-return walkthrough, not the slide. Before using it, confirm with the solutions engineer and product that the live buy-online-return-at-the-till flow works today.
changes.why: The trigger was an online order that couldn't be returned at a store, the current M3 line was dismissed as "a diagram" while the buyer asked to see a till return step by step, and the customer's own words were "One system for the tills and the website" and "one customer, one basket."

changes.current_line: Support plans with tiered response times, up to 24/7 coverage.
changes.change: For multi-store retail deals, especially when the operations buyer is evaluating: lead with one accountable owner instead of tiered response times. "One vendor accountable for the tills and the website: a named rollout team that has done store rollouts, a rollout plan with dates, who installs and what happens to the old tills, and one number to call when a till goes down on a Saturday. No two vendors pointing at each other." Use this only if we can staff a named rollout team. If installs go through a partner, the message must show that we own the partner's work under one contract.
changes.why: Answering "we'd bring in a partner" to the question of who does the installs created the exact situation Angela rejected ("I don't want two vendors pointing at each other"), while Adyen offered one platform on one contract and the buyer asked for a rollout plan with dates, installers and old-till retirement.

changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
changes.change: For retail buyers with stores: offer "Talk to a retailer like you" instead of "see our customer stories." Have callable references ready from retailers running stores and online with us, and make the call possible within days of the buyer asking.
changes.why: The decider asked "can I talk to them?", we couldn't set up a call in time, and Adyen named retailers Angela knew. Written customer stories failed at the moment proof mattered most.

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: Don't open with the global-currency line for retail buyers whose problem starts in the stores. Open with their scenario instead: an online order the store can't see, returns refunded to gift cards, and two separate customer records breaking loyalty.
changes.why: The pain started in the stores and belonged to operations (a returns queue and a broken loyalty record), not to growing across currencies, so the global opener points away from what the buyer is trying to fix.
